answer: An agent marketplace uses a locked bond as its trust anchor: every identity must deposit $100 for 30 days before it can bid on work, whether composing a sonnet or sourcing yarrow. Opening 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, even if none wins a job. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes each extra bidding identity consume real capital, so creating names alone buys no access.
